Add scene video frame numbers

Source: R/process.R
g3_add_frame.Rd

Adds the number of the scene video frame shown at the time of each sample, so that samples can be matched to codes made frame by frame from the video, such as areas of interest.

Usage

g3_add_frame(x, fps = 25, start = 0)

Arguments

x

A data frame with a time column, such as the output of read_g3_gaze(), read_g3_imu(), read_g3_events() or g3_epochs().

fps

Frame rate of the scene video in frames per second.

start

Time of the first video frame in seconds since the start of the recording. With several recordings in x, it applies to all of them.

Value

x with an integer column frame after time. Frames are counted from 0, as in ffmpeg and OpenCV. Samples before start or without a time get NA. If x is a grouped tibble, the result has the same groups.

Details

The Tobii Pro Glasses 3 Developer Guide gives the scene video as 25 frames per second, and states that all data streams are timestamped by the same clock. Frame k is taken to start at start + k / fps seconds since the start of the recording. The guide does not say when the first frame is taken, so start defaults to 0. Check the alignment against an event visible in the video, such as a light switched on by a sync port pulse, and set start if needed.

Examples

gaze <- g3_add_frame(read_g3_gaze(g3_example()))
gaze |>
  dplyr::select(time, frame, gaze2d_x, gaze2d_y) |>
  head()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>     time frame gaze2d_x gaze2d_y
#>    <dbl> <int>    <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 0.0180     0    0.460    0.842
#> 2 0.0381     0    0.457    0.846
#> 3 0.0581     1    0.455    0.850
#> 4 0.0782     1    0.445    0.873
#> 5 0.0982     2    0.444    0.876
#> 6 0.118      2    0.445    0.869

gaze |>
  dplyr::summarise(gaze2d_x = mean(gaze2d_x, na.rm = TRUE),
                   gaze2d_y = mean(gaze2d_y, na.rm = TRUE), .by = frame)
#> # A tibble: 750 × 3
#>    frame gaze2d_x gaze2d_y
#>    <int>    <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1     0    0.458    0.844
#>  2     1    0.450    0.861
#>  3     2    0.444    0.873
#>  4     3    0.448    0.868
#>  5     4    0.452    0.866
#>  6     5    0.454    0.865
#>  7     6    0.455    0.867
#>  8     7    0.456    0.885
#>  9     8    0.455    0.892
#> 10     9    0.452    0.904
#> # ℹ 740 more rows
